content.title: About
content.content: Pickles NFS are classic brined cucumbers seasoned with dill, garlic, and spices. They have a crisp texture, refreshing sour taste, and a subtle aromatic note. The product is made from fresh cucumbers grown in environmentally friendly conditions.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Traditional Russian pickling methods date back over 200 years.
Cucumbers are often blanched in cold water before brining to preserve crunchiness.
Vinegar in the brine helps retain vitamin C and other nutrients.
Mustard seeds are commonly added to the brine for a characteristic flavor.
Pickles are a popular ingredient in salads, sandwiches, and appetizers.

items.title: Low in calories
items.content: A medium pickled cucumber contains about 15 kcal, making it an excellent choice for diet plans.

items.title: Rich in probiotics
items.content: Fermentation creates beneficial bacteria that support gut microbiota.

items.title: Contains vitamin K
items.content: Vitamin K is important for blood clotting and bone health.

items.title: Source of antioxidants
items.content: Cucumbers provide vitamin C and polyphenols that help combat free radicals.

items.title: Supports hydration
items.content: With over 90% water content, pickles help maintain fluid balance.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Excessive salt may be unsuitable for individuals with hypertension.

items.title: Allergy to dill or garlic
items.content: Some people may react to the spices used in the brine.

items.title: Bacterial growth if stored improperly
items.content: Storing pickles above 4 °C for prolonged periods can allow pathogenic bacteria to develop.

items.title: Added sugar in sweet‑sour varieties
items.content: Some recipes contain added sugar, increasing the calorie count.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Pickles can be enjoyed as a snack, added to salads, sandwiches, burgers, or used in cold soups such as okroshka.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep pickles in the refrigerator at 0‑4 °C in their original brine. Once opened, consume within 2‑3 weeks. Discard if mold appears or the smell changes.
